items.name: Readability
items.evidence: No files were written to the project. The decrypt and extract steps ran as one-off `python3 -c` commands, and the only output is recovered.json. There is no committed script to judge for readability.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: No code change exists to judge. Note that the agent left no re-runnable decrypt or extract script, which the project conventions asked for, but there is no code to rate on structure.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No code was persisted. The ad-hoc inline scripts used the XOR key 0x42, but it was derived from the header magic: `753d44c0 ^ 0x42 = 377f0682`.

items.name: Recovery method is principled
items.evidence: The agent derived 0x42 by XORing the header magic and checked the decoded version (3007000) and page size (4096). It decrypted the whole file and let SQLite replay the WAL, testing on copies in /tmp first. It confirmed 11 rows, plus count(*)=11 with a read-only open. It did not run integrity_check.

items.name: Original evidence preserved before in-place repair
items.name_zh: 原地修复前保留原始文件
items.evidence: At step 2 it ran `cp main.db main.db.bak && cp main.db-wal main.db-wal.bak` before anything else. At step 3 a read-write `sqlite3 /app/main.db` open deleted the encrypted WAL, but the backup restored it. The originals were then moved to a scratch dir as orig_main.db-wal.
